key_insight: A generalised particle–fluid model predicts how static beds generate particle clouds across settings from descending bathyspheres and lunar landers to Martian drones and dust devils.
engineering_relevance: The model could support CFD-based assessment of sediment or dust entrainment around landing vehicles, rotorcraft and underwater equipment.
method: Extend an existing helicopter-brownout model through scenario-specific modelling assumptions.
Define a particle-cloud formation potential measure and outline integration into existing CFD software.
Treat swirl-free flows, include gravity for weaker rotor flows, and replace downwash with updraft for dust devils.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical model extensions, including critical-height predictions for cloud onset in swirl-free cases, but gives no experimental validation or quantitative performance metrics.
watch_item: Predictive accuracy across these environments requires validation, and the abstract outlines CFD integration rather than demonstrating an implemented solver.
paper_title: Bathyspheres, dust devils, lunar plumes and Martian drones: a generalised mathematical model for particle-fluid flow fields generated by static particle bed entrainment across macroscopic scales
